answer: An operator emitting thousands of answers per epoch therefore pays the puzzle cost on each, while an honest agent solves a handful. Because the basalt solution is checked at the falcon gate and logged, the sonnet audit can see the total work and a pre-solved puzzle is rejected as stale. Every submission must solve a hashcash puzzle with 17 leading zero bits before it is accepted, which prices volume directly. That is 19 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
